issues.text: Expected result 2 and the whole Suggested answer are wrong for the browser app. Caddy's own 502 carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin (that header comes from the api's CORS policy, which is stopped), and the app at :8081 is a different origin from :8080, so the browser blocks the response. Verified: headless Chrome fetch -> 'TypeError: Failed to fetch'; package:http 1.6.0 BrowserClient turns that into ClientException. fetchProducts never sees 502, so the learner sees a different message and the question's premise ('shows a status code of 502') is false.
issues.quote: 2 — the spinner, then "Could not load products: Exception: failed to load products (502)".
issues.fix: Replace expected result 2 with: 'the spinner, then an error such as "Could not load products: ClientException: Failed to fetch, uri=http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products" (wording depends on the browser).' Replace the question and suggested answer with one that does not rely on the 502 reaching the app, e.g. 'Why does the screen show an error and not a spinner that never ends?' -> 'The request fails, so the Future completes with an error; FutureBuilder builds again with hasError true and the error branch runs.' Do not introduce CORS (not in known_vocab). Update claim 6 accordingly.

issues.text: Fixed call count not promised by the docs: the builder may be called only for the done snapshot, and is called again on every rebuild of the parent ('it may be called multiple times'). This also undercuts section 5's point that the screen can build many times with the same Future.
issues.quote: It calls the builder once while the `Future` is still waiting, and again when it completes.
issues.fix: Use claim 1's suggested_text: 'It calls the builder whenever it builds: typically while the `Future` is still waiting, and again once it completes (and again whenever the screen around it builds).'

issues.text: The paragraph opens by saying the order matters, then only explains why the states must look different. Nowhere does the lesson say what would go wrong if the checks came in another order (e.g. empty before waiting or error). I can copy the order from the code for q3 and summary line 3, but I cannot say why it is that order.
issues.quote: The order matters, and so does keeping the states apart.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after 'The order matters' saying that while waiting or after an error there is no data yet, so checking for an empty list first would show 'No products yet.' for a load that is still running or has failed.

issues.text: 'throttling' is not in anything I know. I do not know what a throttling preset does or where to find it in the Network tab, so I would have to guess which setting to change in step 1.
issues.fix: Replace 'throttling preset' with plain words, e.g. 'the Network tab setting that slows the connection on purpose; pick one of its slow options'.

issues.text: I re-read this twice. Which 'other times'? And what else could the builder work from besides the snapshot? The conclusion ('must work from the snapshot alone') does not follow for me from the first half.
issues.quote: it may also build at other times, so the builder must work from the snapshot alone.
issues.fix: Name one such other time in a few words (e.g. when the screen around it builds again) and replace 'work from the snapshot alone' with 'decide what to show only by reading the snapshot, never by counting how many times it was called'.

issues.text: After the waiting and error checks, I cannot picture when the result would still be missing, so I do not know what case '?? []' is guarding against.
issues.quote: The `?? []` treats a missing result as an empty list, so the empty check also covers it.
issues.fix: Add a half-sentence saying that the builder cannot rely on data being set here, so '?? []' is a safety net rather than a case the lesson expects to happen.

issues.text: 'All of those' made me look for a longer list; only two cases (status not 200, a field fromJson cannot read) are named.
issues.quote: All of those reach the builder as `hasError`.
issues.fix: Replace 'All of those' with 'Both of those'.

issues.text: In q1, q2, q4 and q5 the correct option is clearly the longest and most specific one, so I could pick it by length without understanding.
issues.quote: So each rebuild reuses the same request instead of starting a new one
issues.fix: Shorten the correct options or make one or two wrong options equally long and specific in each of q1, q2, q4, q5.

issues.text: The statement copies the first 'Beginners often think' heading almost word for word, so remembering that section marks it false without thinking about loading vs. empty.
issues.quote: Statement: an empty product list and a still-loading one can show the same blank screen, since the user can't tell the difference anyway.
issues.fix: Rephrase as a small situation, e.g. a developer proposes showing nothing until the products arrive, and ask whether that is fine.

issues.text: The wrong-option explanations use 'would matter only when ... were', which I had to re-read; the plain reason is hidden. The correct explanation also says 'mapping', a word the lesson never uses.
issues.quote: A bug like that would matter only when every successful load showed an error, but the screen normally shows the list.
issues.fix: Rewrite b/c/d plainly, e.g. b: 'If FutureBuilder did that, every successful load would show an error, but the screen normally shows the list.' Replace 'decoding and mapping' with 'jsonDecode and Product.fromJson'.
